name: DURATION
description: DURATION returns the weighted average time until a bond's cash flows are received, measured in years. It is used to estimate interest rate sensitivity.
tldr: Calculates the Macaulay duration of a bond.

parameters.name: frequency
parameters.description: Number of coupon payments per year (1, 2, or 4).

basicExample.explanation: For a 5% coupon bond yielding 6% with semi-annual payments, this returns the Macaulay duration.

advancedExamples.title: With actual/actual basis
advancedExamples.explanation: Basis 1 uses actual days and actual years.

howItWorks: DURATION calculates the Macaulay duration, which is the present-value-weighted average time until cash flows are received. Higher duration means greater sensitivity to interest rate changes.

howToSteps.name: Calculate
howToSteps.text: Press Enter to get the result.

limitations: Does not measure modified duration or convexity.

commonErrors.fix: Use DATE function or valid date serial numbers.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: DURATION works identically in Google Sheets.
googleSheetsEquivalent.notes: Same syntax and behavior as Excel.

faq.question: What is the difference between DURATION and MDURATION?
faq.answer: DURATION is Macaulay duration. MDURATION is modified duration, which directly measures price sensitivity.

faq.question: What does duration measure?
faq.answer: Duration measures the weighted average time to receive cash flows and is used to estimate interest rate risk.
